subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Heaton <sara.heaton@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Sara -

Great to meet you and Tom on the demo today. Thanks for walking through your ingestion flow and real-time assistant use case - helpful context. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the next steps for a Hosted API evaluation and clarify how Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private map to the requirements you mentioned.

1) Quickstart & trial access
- I've attached the Redwood Quickstart (redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf) and a short rate limits spreadsheet.
- We can provision a trial API key scoped to your project (Acme-POC) so your engineers can test with the exact endpoints we demoed.

2) Endpoints & performance notes (Hosted API)
- Base URL: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Streaming: supported via chunked responses (same endpoint, stream=true query param).
- Latency: typical p95 token latency for our curated hosted models is 60-250ms depending on sequence length and model family; we'll share a tailored perf profile once you run a few traces.
- Rate limits: default trial limits are 300 requests/minute and 500k tokens/day. We can temporarily raise the requests/min for evaluation with an SE-approved burst. See attached rate-limits-and-quotas.xlsx.

3) Qualification questions to determine deployment mode
- Isolation & data residency: Do you need tenant-level isolation or on-prem data residency? You mentioned EU data residency for a subset of users - is that for production or just initial POC?
- Throughput & latency SLOs: What concurrent request volume and p95 latency does your product need in production (approx)?
- Compliance & audit: Will Acme require SOC2 + a dedicated audit trail or customer-managed KMS for production?

Guidance summary: based on what you shared, Hosted API is best for a quick evaluation and fast time-to-value. Dedicated capacity is recommended when you want predictable throughput and reserved GPUs for production at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is needed if you must control networking or host keys on-prem.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll spin up an Acme trial key and share endpoints + example cURLs by EOD.
- If you want higher trial rate limits, we can set a short-term increase - let me know target RPS.
- Schedule an SE session with Ethan to walk through prefix caching and batching recommendations once you have traces.

Thanks - happy to jump on a quick sync if that helps.

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0148

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf, rate-limits-and-quotas.xlsx

From: Sara Heaton <sara.heaton@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Thanks Marissa - this is super helpful. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side: 

- Data residency: For the initial POC, EU residency is not required. Production will likely need EU residency for GDPR-sensitive data (we'll confirm in procurement).
- Isolation: We don't strictly need dedicated hardware for POC, but production will need logical separation; not sure yet if Dedicated is required.
- Throughput: Our expected peak is ~150 concurrent requests with bursts up to 500 req/s during campaigns. P95 latency target is <300ms for the assistant paths (short prompts).
- Compliance: Acme requires SOC2 for production and will likely request customer-managed KMS for keys in the Private option.

Question about the trial limits: would a temporary bump to 1000 req/min be possible for the week of the POC? Also - what logging/trace exports do you provide for request-level observability?

Tom and I are available for an SE session Thursday morning PT if Ethan can join.

-
Sara Heaton
Product Manager, AI Platform | Acme Corp
sara.heaton@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Heaton <sara.heaton@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Sara - thanks for the quick answers, this helps a lot.

1) Trial rate limits
- We can provision a temporary increase to 1,000 req/min for a 7-14 day evaluation window. I'll note that as the default for the Acme POC and we can revisit after the first week.

2) Observability / logs
- Hosted API provides request-level telemetry in the Console (per-request latency, token counts, and error traces).
- We can stream request logs to your Splunk/Datadog via an encrypted delivery hook for the trial or provide S3 export of logs for offline analysis.
- Audit logs (who accessed keys, config changes) are included for production tiers; Dedicated/Private add more granular ACL features.

3) Performance & SE session
- Given your burst characteristics, Ethan can walk through batching strategies and prefix caching to reduce cost and keep p95 below 300ms. He'll also suggest appropriate model family choices (low-latency curated models vs higher-quality larger models).

I've provisioned a trial key and created the Acme-POC project in the Console. Next actions:
- I'll send the trial API key in a secure message and the quickstart link (https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart/acme-trial).
- Scheduled SE call: Thursday 14 Apr, 10:00am PT (tentative) - Ethan, can you confirm?
- I'll request the 1,000 req/min bump from our infra team and confirm once approved.

If that sounds good I'll lock the SE session and share calendar invites.

Best,
Marissa
